1. Core Clinical Tension: A 27-year-old female worker from Guangxi with a 4-year history of systemic lupus erythematosus maintained on chronic oral prednisone presents with recurrent fever, profound inflammatory anemia, and suppurative soft tissue ulceration of the right thigh. The clinical picture mimics an active lupus flare (such as cutaneous vasculitis) or secondary bacterial soft-tissue infection (such as staphylococcal cellulitis/septicemia), disguising an invasive opportunistic dimorphic fungal infection.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission triage phase concludes upon readmission physical examination (documenting the 3-cm purulent ulcer and surrounding edematous erythema) and triage laboratory testing (marked anemia, neutrophil leukocytosis, elevated ESR/CRP, positive ANA, normal complements, and negative HIV serology), strictly prior to blood and ulcer secretion microbiological culture isolation of Talaromyces marneffei.
3. Differential Distinctions: Active lupus vasculitis/flare was initially considered due to high-titer ANA and earlier skin histology, but is refuted by normal serum complement levels, normal anti-dsDNA titers, and recurrence into frank suppurative ulceration despite steroid therapy. Bacterial soft-tissue infection and staphylococcal septicemia were considered, but antibacterial regimens produced only temporary benefit without eradicating the deep suppurative ulceration. Definitive fungal blood and exudate cultures confirm disseminated talaromycosis.
case_prompt:
A 27-year-old female factory worker born and residing in Guangxi, China, presents with recurrent right thigh swelling, severe pain, fevers, and cutaneous ulceration. She has a 4-year history of systemic lupus erythematosus managed with maintenance oral prednisone (30 mg daily). Three months earlier, she experienced an initial episode of high fever, pain, and extensive edematous erythema of the right thigh, which transiently abated after hospitalization with glucocorticoids and broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy, but has now recurred with ulcerative progression.

On physical examination, she is febrile with an admission body temperature of 38.8°C. Examination of the right lower extremity demonstrates prominent soft tissue swelling and large scattered patches of edematous erythema, centered on a 3-cm cutaneous ulcer discharging purulent secretions.

Initial triage laboratory evaluation demonstrates severe anemia with a hemoglobin level of 61 g/L and a white blood cell count of 8.93 × 10^9/L with 94.8% neutrophils. Inflammatory markers are markedly elevated, with an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 138 mm/hr and a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 46.8 mg/L. Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) are strongly positive at 109.4 IU/mL. Serum complement levels and anti-dsDNA antibody titers are within normal limits. Serologic testing for HIV antibodies is negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Active Systemic Lupus Erythematosus flare / Lupus vasculitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although the patient had long-standing SLE with high-titer ANA and prior skin histology interpreted as vasculitis, normal complement levels and normal anti-dsDNA titers along with progressive suppurative ulceration despite steroid therapy ruled out an isolated autoimmune flare.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The histopathology of the skin lesions indicated vasculitis, which is consistent with SLE. Active SLE and septicemia were diagnosed.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: While coagulase-negative staphylococci were isolated from initial blood and ulcer cultures, standard antibacterial therapy failed to induce permanent resolution, and the recurrent ulceration was sustained by an underlying invasive dimorphic fungus.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: coagulase-negative Staphylococcus aureus was isolated from ulcer secretions.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: In an immunosuppressed patient from an endemic region with fever, profound anemia, and refractory cutaneous ulceration, microbiological cultures of blood and ulcer secretions isolated the dimorphic fungal pathogen Talaromyces marneffei, with complete clinical resolution upon antifungal therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: T. marneffei was identified in cultures prepared from blood and ulcer secretions

editor_comments: Distillation adheres strictly to the admission breakpoint prior to fungal culture return. No pathogen or final disease spoilers present in the case prompt. All quotes verified verbatim from case text.
